passage.text: When the artists in our town started a street murals project, few residents expected it to grow so quickly. At first, the organisers met in a small room and planned one simple activity involving public walls. They soon discovered that people were more willing to join when they could see a clear benefit for the neighbourhood. The organisers therefore published a short timetable and invited local businesses to offer practical help.

The project was not completely easy. Some volunteers were worried that the work would take too much time, while others wanted to change the plan every week. The team solved this by giving each person one small responsibility and reviewing the results together. This made the project feel manageable, and it also meant that new volunteers could contribute without special experience.

Looking back, the organiser says the most important lesson was not the final result but the way people learned to cooperate. The group still has problems, especially when the weather affects outdoor work, yet members now discuss solutions rather than blaming one another. For this reason, the project has become a useful example of how a modest local idea can create lasting connections.

passage.text: The idea of starting a school newspaper came from a conversation in the canteen one lunchtime. (16) ..... A group of friends complained that there was no way to share news about school events or celebrate students' achievements properly. We wanted to give students a voice and create a platform where achievements in sports, arts and academics could be celebrated by the whole school community on a regular basis.

We approached the head teacher with a proposal, and she gave us permission to publish a monthly edition. (17) ..... She even offered to let us use the printing room after school, which saved us a lot of money and made the project possible. A group of teachers volunteered to supervise the printing sessions, and the art department helped us design a professional logo and layout for the front page of each edition.

Creating the first issue was much more work than we had anticipated at the beginning. (18) ..... We had to write articles, take photographs and design the layout, all while keeping up with our regular studies and homework assignments. Deadlines were tight, and we often had to stay after school to finish editing articles and checking facts before sending the final version to the printer on time.

When the first copies were distributed around the school, the reaction was overwhelmingly positive. (19) ..... Students stopped us in the corridor to say how much they enjoyed reading it and asked when the next issue would be published. The English teacher said the quality of writing had improved significantly since we started, and several students discovered a talent for journalism they did not know they possessed.

The newspaper has now been running successfully for eight months without interruption. (20) ..... We have expanded from four pages to twelve and even started an online version with daily updates about school events. Our online version receives thousands of visits each month from parents, former students and members of the local community who want to stay connected with the school.

passage.text: Our school held a cooking competition last term, and I decided to enter with my best recipe. Each participant had (21) ..... prepare a main course and a dessert using only locally sourced ingredients from the area. I chose to make a vegetable pie (22) ..... a fruit crumble for dessert, both using seasonal produce. The judges were professional chefs from a local restaurant, and they paid close attention (23) ..... every detail of our presentation and cooking technique. My pie was well cooked and tasty, but the crumble (24) ..... a little too sweet for the judges' taste. (25) ..... my surprise, I was still awarded second place out of twenty participants. The experience taught me that cooking requires both creativity (26) ..... discipline to achieve the best possible results. I have started practising new recipes at home every weekend, and my family has been enjoying the opportunity to taste different dishes from around the world that I prepare for them. At the end of the course, each student cooked one dish for the others. Tasting the meals together helped us understand how ingredients and cooking methods change from one country to another.
